note.question: When do guaranteed-margin and low-price contracts imposed by a dominant retailer raise market prices, induce supplier exclusivity, and reduce consumer access?
note.overview: Under the guaranteed-margin regimes, a dominant retailer first selects its margin, the supplier then chooses channel coverage and wholesale terms, and competing retailers subsequently set prices; in the wholesale benchmark, the supplier moves first. The paper derives subgame-perfect outcomes by backward induction under all three regimes.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In Models M and ML, focal retailer 1 first chooses its guaranteed margin alpha. The supplier then chooses whether to partner with both retailers or exclusively and sets wholesale price w; served retailers next set retail prices, after which demand and profits are realized. Model ML adds the supplier-funded low-price-guarantee rule. In benchmark Model W there is no retailer contract stage: the supplier first selects coverage and w, followed by retail pricing.
